title: Styling a Quarto Website with CSS/SCSS
section: CSS vs. SCSS in plain terms
text:
CSS vs. SCSS in plain terms
CSS is the language browsers use to style a page. Each rule names an element and says how it should look.
SCSS (Sass) is CSS with extra tools. The two that matter most for Quarto:

Variables. Define a color once as $brand-teal and reuse it everywhere. Change it in one place and the whole site updates.
Nesting. Write a hover style inside the rule it belongs to instead of repeating the selector.

Quarto themes are built on Bootstrap, which is written in SCSS. That’s why an SCSS file can do more than a CSS file: it can change the theme’s settings before the theme is built, instead of overriding it afterward.

title: Styling a Quarto Website with CSS/SCSS
text:
Step 1: Connect the SCSS file
The theme is set in _quarto.yml. Listing two items layers my file on top of the Cosmo theme:


_quarto.yml

format:
  html:
    theme:
      light: [cosmo, custom.scss]

section: What I’d tell someone starting out
text:
What I’d tell someone starting out






TipPractical tips




Start with a built in theme and only change what bothers you. Most of this site’s look comes from five variables.
Put colors in variables first. Retyping hex codes leads to slightly different teals on different pages.
Use the browser’s Inspect tool (right click any element) to find the class name you need to target.
Keep one SCSS file for the whole site and link it in _quarto.yml, so every page stays consistent.

title: CEP Dashboard
text:
What the data shows


Employees are the strength
Members rate staff highly. Courtesy (4.35 out of 5) and helpfulness (4.31) lead, with professionalism and availability close behind at 4.08.


Overall satisfaction is strong
84% of members who gave a rating called the credit union Excellent or Good, and only 3 members rated it Poor or Very Poor.


Rates are the biggest opportunity
“Rates are lower than at other institutions” scored 3.06, the lowest of any statement. That points to a messaging or pricing gap worth digging into.


Loan applications vary by location
Headquarters members gave employees a higher score (4.28 vs. 4.14) but found loan applications less simple (3.28 vs. 3.61) than members at other locations.

title: CEP Dashboard
text:
How it was built
The dashboard is a single Quarto file using format: dashboard. Python reads the SPSS file with pyreadstat, pandas calculates the averages and percentages, and plotly draws the interactive charts. Value boxes, rows, and pages are all set with Quarto’s dashboard layout syntax:
format:
  dashboard:
    orientation: rows
# Overview          <- a page (tab) of the dashboard
## Row {height=26%} <- a row of cards on that page
When the CEP data arrives, the same structure can be pointed at the Collins College admissions and survey data with only the column names changing.

title: Listings in Quarto
text:
A Listing is a Quarto feature that builds a page of links to other pages automatically. Instead of hand typing a list of projects and updating it every time something new is added, you point the Listing at a folder. Quarto reads each file’s title, description, image, and categories, then builds the cards for you.
For a portfolio, that means adding a new project is as simple as dropping a new .qmd file into the projects/ folder. The cards, the filters, and the sorting all update on the next render.

title: Listings in Quarto
text:
How this Listing is built

1. Each project is its own page
Every card above comes from a file in projects/. The YAML at the top is what the Listing reads:


projects/google-ads.qmd

---
title: "Google Ads Turnaround: 3x Monthly Leads"
description: "Rebuilding a lead generation account by fixing the bidding strategy order."
image: images/google-ads.png
categories: [Google Ads, PPC, Lead Generation]
order: 2
---



2. The Listing page tells Quarto what to collect
The YAML on this page sets where to look and how to display what it finds:


listings.qmd

listing:
  - id: project-grid
    contents: projects/*.qmd     # every .qmd file in the folder
    type: grid                   # cards in columns
    sort: "order"                # uses the order field in each file
    categories: unnumbered       # adds the clickable category filter
    fields: [image, title, description, categories]
    grid-columns: 3



3. A div marks where it appears
The id connects the settings to a spot on the page, so one page can hold more than one Listing:
::: {#project-grid}
:::

Why Listings work well for a portfolio


Easy to grow
New work goes in a new file. Nothing else on the site needs editing.


Easy to browse

Consistent

title: Google Ads Turnaround: 3x Monthly Leads
text:
Role: PPC Analyst, Unbiazed LLC
Account: Waste management lead generation

title: Google Ads Turnaround: 3x Monthly Leads
text:
The problem
I inherited the account on a Maximize Conversions bid strategy, but it didn’t have enough conversion data for Google’s automated bidding to learn from. Volume stayed low.

title: Google Ads Turnaround: 3x Monthly Leads
text:
What I changed

Switched to Maximize Clicks to build traffic and give the account conversion history.
Watched conversion volume until there was enough data to support smart bidding.
Moved back to conversion based bidding once the data could carry it.

title: Google Ads Turnaround: 3x Monthly Leads
text:
The result
Monthly leads roughly tripled. The lesson: automated bidding needs data first, so sometimes the fastest route to more conversions is to stop optimizing for them for a while.
